backend.explanation: The four obsolete fixture expectations were corrected; all affected files were rerun (29 tests). Production source did not change after the full run.

reports.name: registration-results
checks: Private expiring initialization URL binds the first owner to a verified provider identity without a code form
Add Hub URL exposes parallel configured provider buttons; owner sees computers but has no implicit usage or agent creation grant
Reloadable Hub credentials use standard rotating OAuth refresh sessions without a browser signing-key database
Temporary refresh outage preserves the saved account and recovers without provider reauthentication
A registered identity remains a nonmember until a targeted invitation; Admin status grants management without Computer usage
An Admin-only browser sees computers without usage, invites normal Members, and has no admin-promotion or owner-policy controls
Parallel identities remain connected and shared Computer and agent resources are deduplicated across explicit allowlists
A mutation selects one write-authorized identity and dispatches once without retrying another identity
Owner sign-in policy blocks and reallows a saved Feishu OAuth session without deleting or recreating the identity
Fresh provider authentication replaces only that identity session while other identities stay connected

steps.name: Two independent browser accounts sign in
Owner creates a hub and downloads pairing; real Computer CLI attaches and connects outbound
Agent creation and live conversation traverse the outbound computer connection
Computer shutdown preserves the browser draft and reports offline
Computer restart restores persisted agent history and sending
Hub membership alone does not expose computer agents
Hub membership and an explicit Computer allowlist entry enable creation and sending
Removing a Computer allowlist entry immediately disables an open agent
Legacy retention policies cannot bypass the explicit Computer allowlist
Revoked member sees no Computers or agent creation targets
Two computers attach independently to one hub and route to distinct runtimes
Mobile computer drawer opens and closes; viewport has no horizontal overflow

reports.name: distributed-results
steps: Fixture authenticated session, PKCE hub cookie exchange, single-use enrollment and relayed conversation
One account uses two independently running hubs without sharing agent state
Returning to a hub restores only its own unsent draft
Second account sees only its invited hub and no ungranted computers
Optional authority sign-in has no password/code fallback and reports missing provider configuration
No uncaught browser errors in the separate-service flow

reports.name: agent-creation-results
checks: An already-controlled tab upgrades the old worker before rendering; Hubs & computers loads working controls instead of the static-client error
Configured provider, model and reasoning are selected as real values, with disabled placeholders and no generic default option
Independent client opens Pi/Codex/Claude creation; provider-specific Pi models and reasoning reach the service worker launch request
Codex maps ChatGPT authentication and Fast correctly; changing models removes unsupported reasoning
Claude Code supports custom model and reasoning without inheriting another runtime's provider or Fast setting
pi: private endpoint, masked key, custom model and advanced controls reach the launch; switching providers clears credentials
codex: private endpoint, masked key, custom model and advanced controls reach the launch; switching providers clears credentials
cc: private endpoint, masked key, custom model and advanced controls reach the launch; switching providers clears credentials
Unknown configured provider or model stays unselected and cannot create an agent with empty launch values
Switching computers clears previous selections and paths; late catalog responses cannot replace current choices
Keyboard focus wraps within creation; Escape preserves dialog; invalid names focus their associated alert; pending launch announces status and locks choices
Account/workspace form submits the actual configured provider, model and reasoning; all three runtime forms fit 390px and cancel restores focus
Resume selects a scoped saved session or explicit ID, clears IDs on runtime changes, and sends no saved credentials

reports.name: invitation-results
checks: Owner creates Google and tenant-specific Feishu invitations using the actual mobile Manage access form
No provider account gains access before accepting an invitation; malformed codes display an error
An unrelated Google identity cannot redeem a Feishu invitation
Google and Feishu users accept through the actual invitation screen with verified provider identities
Reusing a redeemed code displays an error without another membership change
Agent sharing cannot bypass the required Computer allowlist, including operator shares
Two browser accounts verify explicit Computer read/write grants and revocation; an agent share cannot elevate read-only or removed Computer access
Actual hub Sign-in methods copies the exact connection, identity and tenant for an invitation
Fresh client offers an empty Add Hub URL field with no preset Hub or setup code
Manually entered Hub advertises a separate allowed Feishu OAuth button without device-key or setup-code controls
Client stays within390px and creates no device signing-key database
client.providerAuthorization: Not performed; provider button was only inspected

checks: Public HTTPS Hub advertises its sole configured Feishu app
Private initialization link opens Hub-owned provider login in mobile browser
Provider handoff uses Hub callback and PKCE without exposing secret
hub.providerLogin: Not performed: intercepted at provider handoff; actual user authorization still required

live.ownerInitialization: Private link generated, expires after24h; not consumed by probes. User must complete provider sign-in.
live.google: Supported and tested with controlled OAuth; no real Google app credentials supplied.
live.feishu: Configured team app retained. Verified identity from earlier real login retained. Public initialization and PKCE handoff pass; owner callback requires user sign-in.

removed: Human device signing keys and enrollment/challenge routes
rules: Private expiring single-use initialization callback assigns Owner atomically
Every user needs explicit Computer allowlist including owners/admins
All signed identities contribute concurrently without merging accounts or duplicating dispatch
